docs.title: Feedback Configuration
docs.text: The Ansible Backstage plugins provide a configurable feedback system that allows users to submit sentiment feedback about their experience. This feature can be enabled or disabled through the Backstage configuration.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: The feedback system is controlled by the ansible.feedback.enabled configuration option in your app-config.yaml file.

docs.title: Default Configuration
docs.text: By default, the feedback system is disabled completely. If no configuration is provided, the feedback forms will not be displayed.

docs.title: Configuration Options
docs.text:
ansible:
  feedback:
    enabled: false

When disabled:

  • The feedback floating action button (FAB) will not be displayed
  • Users will not be able to access the feedback modal
  • No feedback forms will be rendered in the UI

docs.title: Enabling Feedback
docs.text:
To enable the feedback system, set the enabled option to true:

ansible:
  feedback:
    enabled: true

docs.title: Where Feedback Appears
docs.text:
The feedback system appears in two locations:

  1. Self-Service Plugin: A floating feedback button in the bottom-right corner of the self-service interface
  2. Backstage RHAAP Plugin: A floating feedback button in the bottom-right corner of the Ansible page

docs.title: What Feedback Captures
docs.text:
When enabled, the feedback system captures:

  • User Rating: A 1-5 star rating system
  • Feedback Text: Detailed user comments about their experience
  • Consent: User acknowledgment that feedback is shared with Red Hat

docs.title: Analytics Integration
docs.text:
When feedback is submitted, it sends analytics events to the configured analytics provider:

analytics.captureEvent('feedback', 'sentiment', {
  attributes: {
    type: 'sentiment',
    ratings: number, // 1-5 star rating
    feedback: string, // user's detailed feedback
  },
});

docs.title: Privacy and Compliance
docs.text:
The feedback system includes:

  • Explicit consent checkbox
  • Link to Red Hat's Privacy Policy
  • Clear indication that feedback is shared with Red Hat for product improvement

docs.title: Configuration Examples
docs.text:
ansible:
  feedback:
    enabled: true # Default set to disabled

docs.title: Feedback Button Not Appearing
docs.text:
1. Check that ansible.feedback.enabled is set to true in your configuration
  2. Verify the configuration is properly loaded by checking the browser's developer tools
  3. Ensure you're using a recent version of the Ansible Backstage plugins

docs.title: Configuration Not Taking Effect
docs.text:
1. Restart the Backstage backend after changing configuration
  2. Clear browser cache and refresh the frontend
  3. Check for YAML syntax errors in your configuration file

docs.title: Related Documentation
docs.text:
• Self-Service Plugin Documentation
  • Backstage RHAAP Plugin Documentation

docs.title: Home Template Listing (AAP-First Visibility)
docs.text:
The Self-Service Templates home page lists catalog templates the signed-in user is allowed to run in Ansible Automation Platform (AAP). Visibility is driven by the user's live AAP job-template permissions, not only by what was synced into the catalog.

This complements Job Template Synchronization, which imports templates from AAP on a schedule. The home page answers a different question: which of those catalog entries can this user execute right now?

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Concern Mechanism What the user can run in AAP GET /api/auth/rhaap/user-job-templates What exists in the catalog queryEntities with a server-side filter predicate Session / token for AAP rhAapAuthApi.getAccessToken() → X-RHAAP-Access-Token header Stable list across navigation JobTemplatesProvider caches IDs at the route level

docs.title: Key behaviors
docs.text:
• AAP-backed templates (metadata.aapJobTemplateId set) appear only when that ID is in the user's current AAP job-template list.
  • SCM / non-AAP templates (no aapJobTemplateId) always pass the visibility filter.
  • The catalog query runs only after the AAP list fetch succeeds (loadState === 'ready'). On failure, the page shows an error with Retry instead of falling back to SCM-only results.
  • Pagination is server-side (default page size 20; options 10, 20, 50, 100).

For adding SCM or other external providers, see Extensibility.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
  participant UI as Home page
  participant Provider as JobTemplatesProvider
  participant AuthApi as rhAapAuthApi
  participant AnsibleApi as AnsibleApiClient
  participant Backend as auth /rhaap/user-job-templates
  participant AAP as AAP API
  participant Catalog as catalog queryEntities

  UI->>Provider: mount / navigate back
  Provider->>AnsibleApi: getUserJobTemplates()
  AnsibleApi->>AuthApi: getAccessToken()
  AuthApi-->>AnsibleApi: AAP access token
  AnsibleApi->>Backend: GET + X-RHAAP-Access-Token
  Backend->>AAP: GET job_templates (user token)
  AAP-->>Backend: template IDs
  Backend-->>Provider: { items: [{ id, name }] }
  Provider-->>UI: jobTemplateIds, loadState ready
  UI->>Catalog: queryEntities($all visibility + filters)
  Catalog-->>UI: paginated Template entities

docs.title: Backend: user job templates endpoint
docs.text:
Route: GET /api/auth/rhaap/user-job-templates

Module: auth-backend-module-rhaap-provider (userJobTemplatesRouter.ts)

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
1. Backstage user session — httpAuth.credentials(req, { allow: ['user'] }). Unauthenticated callers receive 401.
  2. AAP access token — resolved in this order:
  3. X-RHAAP-Access-Token request header (preferred; sent by the Self-Service frontend).
  4. rhaap-refresh-token cookie — refresh via rhAAPAuthenticate, then call AAP. Used when no header is present (for example direct API use).

The route is registered with allow: 'unauthenticated' on the auth HTTP router so the handler can perform its own httpAuth check; callers still need a valid Backstage session.

docs.title: Response
docs.text:
{
  "items": [{ "id": 42, "name": "Deploy application" }]
}

IDs come from ansibleService.getResourceData('job_templates', accessToken) using the same org/label filters as catalog sync (see job-templates.md).

docs.title: Error responses
docs.text: Status Typical cause 401 No Backstage session, missing/invalid AAP token, or invalid_grant on refresh 502 AAP unreachable or unexpected failure after token resolution

docs.title: API client
docs.text:
AnsibleApiClient.getUserJobTemplates() (plugins/self-service/src/apis.ts):

  1. Calls rhAapAuthApi.getAccessToken().
  2. Sends X-RHAAP-Access-Token on the request to the auth plugin base URL.
  3. Maps invalid_grant (and empty token) to: Your AAP sign-in session expired. Sign out and sign in again.

AAPApis factory depends on rhAapAuthApiRef so the client always has access to the OAuth session.

docs.title: JobTemplatesProvider
docs.text:
Wraps template routes so AAP IDs survive remounts when navigating away and back.

State UI loading Skeleton placeholders ready Catalog list with visibility predicate error Message + Retry (does not query catalog)

Mount points:

  • RouteView.tsx — layout route for /self-service/catalog and template detail (dev app yarn start).
  • Home.tsx — TemplatesRoutesPage wrapper for production-style routing.

docs.title: Catalog visibility predicate
docs.text:
buildVisibilityPredicate(jobTemplateIds) (buildVisibilityPredicate.ts):

$any:
  - metadata.aapJobTemplateId does not exist     # SCM templates
  - metadata.aapJobTemplateId $in [user's IDs]  # AAP templates user can run

buildHomeTemplateCatalogQuery combines this with category/tag/owner/source filters via $all.

If jobTemplateIds is empty (should not happen in ready state), only SCM templates would match — which is why the UI blocks the catalog query until the AAP fetch succeeds.

docs.title: Pagination
docs.text: Constants in constants.ts: default PAGE_SIZE = 20, options [10, 20, 50, 100]. Footer shows range (1–20 of N), page size selector, and prev/next controls.

docs.title: Routing notes
docs.text:
Environment Entry Provider location Local dev (packages/app, yarn start) SelfServicePage → RouteView RouteView layout <Route> Dynamic plugin / RHDH Plugin route tree TemplatesRoutesPage in Home.tsx

Both paths must wrap template catalog routes in JobTemplatesProvider. Otherwise useJobTemplates throws or the list refetches with empty IDs on every remount.

docs.title: Extensibility (SCM and future providers)
docs.text: The current implementation is the first provider (AAP). The same pattern applies to SCM, workflows, orchestrator, or any external system where catalog sync alone is not enough to decide what a user can run.

docs.title: Two layers of visibility
docs.text:
Every template on the home page passes through two independent checks:

Layer Question Mechanism Catalog access Is this entity in the catalog and readable by the user? Backstage catalog RBAC / permission plugin (unchanged) Source access Does the user have permission in the external system right now? Per-provider resolver (AAP today; others optional)

Source access only matters for templates tied to an external system. Templates with no external ID rely on catalog access alone.

docs.title: How sources differ today
docs.text:
Source ansible.com/template-source External ID Live permission API AAP job template aap-template metadata.aapJobTemplateId GET /api/auth/rhaap/user-job-templates SCM scm (or unset / legacy) None None — catalog RBAC only Future (workflow, orchestrator, …) TBD per taxonomy TBD per provider TBD per provider

SCM templates pass the visibility filter because they have no aapJobTemplateId — see the $exists: false branch in buildVisibilityPredicate. That is intentional: sync already controls which SCM templates enter the catalog, and catalog RBAC gates who can read them.

SourcePicker filters by ansible.com/template-source for UX only. It is not an authorization boundary.

docs.title: What generalizes without rewrites
docs.text:
These pieces are provider-agnostic and should stay stable as new sources are added:

  1. Route-level cache — JobTemplatesProvider can evolve into a TemplateVisibilityProvider that holds allow-lists and load state per source.
  2. Composed catalog query — buildHomeTemplateCatalogQuery already combines predicates with $all; each provider contributes one branch.
  3. Source taxonomy — ansible.com/template-source identifies which branch applies to an entity.
  4. Load-then-query — Do not call queryEntities until resolvers that block listing (today: AAP) reach ready or surface a clear error.

docs.title: Per-provider contract
docs.text:
When adding a source that needs live external permissions, implement this checklist:

# Deliverable Notes 1 template-source value e.g. aap-template, scm, aap-workflow, orchestrator 2 Stable external ID on entity One canonical metadata field or annotation (e.g. metadata.aapJobTemplateId, or ansible.com/scm-repo-ref for SCM) 3 Backend resolver resolveVisibleIds(user) → string[] — one route per provider is fine; avoid a single mega-endpoint 4 Auth for upstream API User OAuth token, app installation, or service account — same header/cookie patterns as AAP where applicable 5 Predicate branch buildXVisibilityPredicate(ids) — one $any branch keyed on source + ID field 6 Frontend fetch + cache Register in the route-level provider; expose loadState / errorMessage / refresh 7 Error UX Per-provider re-auth messaging (e.g. AAP invalid_grant → sign out and sign in)

docs.title: Composed visibility predicate
docs.text:
Today (AAP + SCM passthrough):

$any:
  - metadata.aapJobTemplateId does not exist          # SCM / non-AAP
  - metadata.aapJobTemplateId $in [user AAP IDs]    # AAP

With multiple live providers, merge branches — one endpoint per provider, one predicate branch per source:

visibility = $all [
  kind = Template,
  user filters (category, tag, owner, source picker, …),
  $any [
    # No external ID — catalog RBAC is sufficient
    { externalIdField: { $exists: false } },

    # AAP job templates
    { $and: [
        { 'metadata.annotations.ansible.com/template-source': 'aap-template' },
        { 'metadata.aapJobTemplateId': { $in: aapIds } }
      ]
    },

    # SCM (only if live repo ACL is required later)
    { $and: [
        { 'metadata.annotations.ansible.com/template-source': 'scm' },
        { 'metadata.annotations.ansible.com/scm-repo-ref': { $in: scmRefs } }
      ]
    },

    # Future providers follow the same shape
  ]
]

NOTE: Tighten the SCM passthrough branch once SCM gets a live resolver — scope the $exists: false case to entities that genuinely have no external ACL, or gate by template-source so AAP entities never fall through by accident.

docs.title: SCM: today vs later
docs.text:
Today (no code change required): SCM visibility = in catalog + user can read the entity. No second API call.

Later (if repo-level ACL matters): Add an SCM resolver parallel to AAP:

  • Backend calls GitHub/GitLab (or similar) with the user's SCM token or an installation token.
  • Returns repo refs or template keys the user can access.
  • Catalog entities carry a matching ansible.com/scm-repo-ref (or equivalent).
  • Predicate branch filters SCM templates to that allow-list.

docs.title: Multi-provider flow (target shape)
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
  participant UI as Home page
  participant Provider as TemplateVisibilityProvider
  participant Resolvers as Per-source resolvers
  participant Catalog as catalog queryEntities

  UI->>Provider: mount
  par AAP resolver
    Provider->>Resolvers: fetch AAP IDs
    Resolvers-->>Provider: aapIds
  and SCM resolver (optional)
    Provider->>Resolvers: fetch SCM refs
    Resolvers-->>Provider: scmRefs
  end
  Provider-->>UI: all ready / per-source errors
  UI->>Catalog: queryEntities(composed predicate)
  Catalog-->>UI: paginated Template entities

Resolvers can run in parallel. Block the catalog query only for sources marked required (AAP is required today because an empty AAP list would hide all AAP templates incorrectly).

docs.title: "Could not load your AAP job templates" / session expired
docs.text:
Symptom: Error on the Templates home page; backend logs may show user-job-templates token refresh failed or invalid_grant.

Cause: The AAP OAuth refresh token or access token is stale while the Backstage session still appears signed in. Common after AAP restarts, OAuth app changes, or long idle periods.

Fix:

  1. Sign out of the portal (RHAAP provider).
  2. Sign in again to obtain fresh OAuth tokens.
  3. Use Retry only after a new sign-in — retry alone does not fix invalid_grant.

docs.title: Only SCM templates visible after navigation
docs.text:
Symptom: After leaving Templates and returning, only non-AAP templates appear.

Cause (historical): jobTemplates state lived inside HomeComponent and reset on remount; catalog queried with jobTemplateIds = [].

Fix: Ensure JobTemplatesProvider wraps the route (see Routing notes). Do not render the catalog until loadState === 'ready'.

docs.title: useJobTemplates must be used within JobTemplatesProvider
docs.text:
Cause: A template page renders outside the provider tree (often a new route added without the layout wrapper).

Fix: Add JobTemplatesProvider to the parent layout route for all template catalog paths.

docs.title: Backend returns 401 but user looks logged in
docs.text:
Check:

  1. Browser request to /api/auth/rhaap/user-job-templates includes X-RHAAP-Access-Token.
  2. Backstage session cookie is sent (credentials: 'include').
  3. AAP OAuth app redirect URI matches backend.baseUrl (see External Authentication).
  4. User has permission to list job templates in AAP for the configured org(s).

docs.title: Debug logging
docs.text:
backend:
  logging:
    level: debug

Look for:

  • user-job-templates token refresh failed — auth provider / cookie path
  • user-job-templates failed — AAP API call after token resolution

docs.title: Job Template Synchronization
docs.text: The Job Template Synchronization feature enables automatic import and synchronization of job templates from Ansible Automation Platform (AAP) into Backstage. This integration creates executable templates in the Backstage catalog, allowing users to launch AAP job templates directly from the Backstage interface.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Job templates from AAP are synchronized as Backstage Template entities with the scaffolder.backstage.io/v1beta3 API version. Each job template becomes an executable template that users can run through Backstage's scaffolder interface, providing a self-service automation experience.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Automatic Synchronization: Job templates are automatically imported from AAP on a configurable schedule
  • Survey Integration: Job templates with surveys are supported with dynamic form generation
  • Filtering Options: Sync can be filtered by organization, labels, and survey status
  • Direct Execution: Templates can be launched directly from Backstage with AAP OAuth2 integration
  • Real-time Status: Job execution status and results are displayed in Backstage

docs.title: Basic Configuration
docs.text:
Add the following configuration to your app-config.yaml:

catalog:
  providers:
    rhaap:
      development:
        orgs: SIG-IDE # Organization name(s) to sync from
        sync:
          jobTemplates:
            enabled: true
            schedule:
              frequency: { minutes: 60 }
              timeout: { minutes: 15 }

docs.title: Advanced Configuration Options
docs.text:
catalog:
  providers:
    rhaap:
      development:
        orgs: SIG-IDE
        sync:
          jobTemplates:
            enabled: true
            schedule:
              frequency: { minutes: 60 }
              timeout: { minutes: 15 }
            # Optional: Filter by survey status
            surveyEnabled: true # true, false, or omit for all
            # Optional: Filter by labels
            labels:
              - production
              - self-service
              - approved

docs.title: Configuration Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description enabled boolean Yes Enable/disable job template synchronization schedule.frequency object Yes How often to sync (e.g., { minutes: 60 }) schedule.timeout object Yes Maximum sync duration (e.g., { minutes: 15 }) surveyEnabled boolean No Filter templates by survey status labels array No Filter templates by specific labels

docs.title: Multiple Organizations
docs.text:
To sync from multiple organizations:

catalog:
  providers:
    rhaap:
      development:
        orgs:
          - SIG-IDE
          - DevOps-Team
          - QA-Team
        sync:
          jobTemplates:
            enabled: true
            schedule:
              frequency: { minutes: 60 }
              timeout: { minutes: 15 }

docs.title: Entity Structure
docs.text:
Job templates are synchronized as Backstage Template entities with the following structure:

apiVersion: scaffolder.backstage.io/v1beta3
kind: Template
metadata:
  namespace: default
  name: my-job-template
  title: 'My Job Template'
  description: 'Description from AAP job template'
  aapJobTemplateId: 123
  tags:
    - ansible
    - automation
    - production
  annotations:
    backstage.io/managed-by-location: 'url:https://aap.example.com/execution/templates/job-template/123/details'
    backstage.io/managed-by-origin-location: 'url:https://aap.example.com/execution/templates/job-template/123/details'
spec:
  type: service
  parameters:
    - title: 'Job Configuration'
      required:
        - token
      properties:
        token:
          title: Token
          type: string
          ui:field: AAPTokenField
          ui:widget: hidden
        # Additional parameters based on job template configuration
  steps:
    - id: launch-job
      name: 'My Job Template'
      action: rhaap:launch-job-template
      input:
        token: ''${{ parameters.token }}''
        values:
          template: 'My Job Template'
          # Additional input values
  output:
    text:
      - title: 'Job executed successfully'
        content: |
          **Job ID:** ${{ steps['launch-job'].output.data.id }}
          **Job STATUS:** ${{ steps['launch-job'].output.data.status }}

docs.title: Metadata Fields
docs.text:
• name: Sanitized job template name (spaces and special characters converted to hyphens)
  • title: Original job template name from AAP
  • description: Job template description from AAP
  • aapJobTemplateId: AAP job template ID for reference
  • tags: Labels from AAP converted to Backstage tags
  • annotations: Links back to the original AAP job template

docs.title: Dynamic Form Generation
docs.text: The plugin automatically generates forms based on job template configuration:

docs.title: Standard Parameters
docs.text:
All job templates include these parameters:

  • Token: OAuth2 token (automatically populated, hidden from user)
  • Job Type: Run or Check mode (if ask_job_type_on_launch is enabled)
  • Inventory: Target inventory (if ask_inventory_on_launch is enabled)
  • Credentials: Required credentials (if ask_credential_on_launch is enabled)
  • Execution Environment: EE selection (if ask_execution_environment_on_launch is enabled)
  • Verbosity: Ansible verbosity level (if ask_verbosity_on_launch is enabled)
  • Tags: Job tags (if ask_tags_on_launch is enabled)
  • Skip Tags: Tags to skip (if ask_skip_tags_on_launch is enabled)
  • Limit: Host limit pattern (if ask_limit_on_launch is enabled)
  • Extra Variables: Additional variables (if ask_variables_on_launch is enabled)

docs.title: Survey Integration
docs.text:
Job templates with surveys automatically include survey questions as form fields:

# Example survey integration
parameters:
  - title: 'Survey Questions'
    properties:
      target_environment:
        title: 'Target Environment'
        description: 'Select deployment environment'
        type: string
        enum: ['dev', 'staging', 'prod']
        default: 'dev'
      confirmation:
        title: 'Confirm Execution'
        description: "Type 'yes' to confirm"
        type: string
        pattern: '^yes$'

docs.title: By Survey Status
docs.text:
Filter job templates based on whether they have surveys enabled:

# Sync only templates with surveys
surveyEnabled: true

# Sync only templates without surveys
surveyEnabled: false

# Sync all templates (default)
# surveyEnabled: (omit this field)

docs.title: By Labels
docs.text:
Filter job templates by specific labels:

labels:
  - production
  - self-service
  - approved

This configuration will sync only job templates that have at least one of the specified labels.

docs.title: By Exclude Labels
docs.text:
Exclude job templates with specific labels:

excludeLabels:
  - deprecated
  - experimental
  - internal-only

This configuration will exclude job templates that have any of the specified labels from synchronization.

Implementation Details:

  • The plugin first attempts to use the AAP API parameter not__labels__name__in for server-side filtering
  • If the API doesn't support this parameter, client-side filtering is applied as a fallback
  • This ensures compatibility across different AAP versions

Note: You can use both labels and excludeLabels together. The labels filter is applied first (include only templates with these labels), then the excludeLabels filter is applied (exclude templates with these labels from the result).

docs.title: By Organization
docs.text:
Filter by AAP organization:

# Single organization
orgs: SIG-IDE

# Multiple organizations
orgs:
  - SIG-IDE
  - DevOps-Team

docs.title: Discovering Job Templates
docs.text:
1. Navigate to Create → Choose a template in Backstage
  2. Job templates appear with the "service" type
  3. Filter by tags to find specific automation templates
  4. Templates show AAP-specific metadata and descriptions

docs.title: Executing Job Templates
docs.text:
1. Select a job template from the template catalog
  2. Fill out the generated form with required parameters
  3. Review configuration in the final step
  4. Click "Create" to launch the job in AAP
  5. View job execution results and status

docs.title: Monitoring Execution
docs.text:
After launching a job template:

  • Job ID: Unique identifier for the AAP job
  • Status: Current execution status (pending, running, successful, failed)
  • Output: Links to detailed job logs in AAP (if configured)

docs.title: Common Issues
docs.text:
Templates not appearing in catalog:

  • Check AAP connectivity and token permissions
  • Verify organization names match exactly
  • Review filter criteria (labels, survey status)
  • Check sync schedule and logs

Form fields missing:

  • Ensure job template has "Prompt on Launch" options enabled in AAP
  • Verify survey is properly configured and enabled
  • Check for survey specification errors

Job launch failures:

  • Verify OAuth2 configuration between Backstage and AAP
  • Check user permissions in AAP
  • Ensure required credentials are available
  • Validate inventory and execution environment access

docs.title: Logging
docs.text:
Enable debug logging to troubleshoot sync issues:

backend:
  logging:
    level: debug

Look for log entries from:

  • plugin-catalog-rh-aap: Job template provider logs
  • backstage-rhaap-common: AAP client logs

docs.title: Manual Sync Trigger
docs.text:
To manually trigger a sync (useful for testing):

  1. Access the catalog backend API
  2. Call the refresh endpoint for the job template provider
  3. Monitor logs for sync progress and errors

docs.title: Token Management
docs.text:
• Job templates use OAuth2 tokens for AAP authentication
  • Tokens are automatically managed by the auth provider
  • Users don't need to provide AAP credentials directly

docs.title: RBAC Integration
docs.text:
• Job template access respects AAP RBAC policies
  • Users can only see and execute templates they have permissions for
  • Backstage RBAC can provide additional access controls

docs.title: Audit Trail
docs.text:
• All job executions are logged in both Backstage and AAP
  • Job IDs provide traceability between systems
  • User attribution is maintained through OAuth2 integration

docs.title: Template Organization
docs.text:
• Use consistent labeling in AAP for better filtering
  • Group related templates with common labels
  • Provide clear descriptions for self-service users

docs.title: Survey Design
docs.text:
• Keep surveys simple and user-friendly
  • Use validation patterns for critical inputs
  • Provide helpful descriptions and examples

docs.title: Sync Configuration
docs.text:
• Set appropriate sync frequency (avoid too frequent syncing)
  • Use filtering to limit templates to relevant ones
  • Monitor sync performance and adjust timeouts as needed

docs.title: User Experience
docs.text:
• Train users on template discovery and execution
  • Provide documentation for complex templates
  • Set up monitoring for failed job executions

docs.title: Scaffolder Action
docs.text:
The plugin provides the rhaap:launch-job-template scaffolder action:

- id: launch-job
  name: Launch Job Template
  action: rhaap:launch-job-template
  input:
    token: string # OAuth2 token
    values:
      template: string # Job template name
      inventory: object # Inventory selection
      credentials: array # Credential selection
      extraVariables: object # Additional variables
      # ... other job template parameters

docs.title: Configuration Schema
docs.text:
The plugin validates configuration against the following schema:

interface JobTemplateConfig {
  enabled: boolean;
  schedule: {
    frequency: { minutes: number } | { hours: number } | { days: number };
    timeout: { minutes: number } | { hours: number };
  };
  surveyEnabled?: boolean;
  labels?: string[];
}

docs.title: Catalog sync HTTP routes (operators and integrations)
docs.text:
If you call the catalog backend manually to trigger AAP sync (for example from a script or external dashboard), use:

  • GET <catalog-base>/ansible/sync/from-aap/orgs_users_teams
  • GET <catalog-base>/ansible/sync/from-aap/job_templates

These replace the previous /aap/sync_orgs_users_teams and /aap/sync_job_templates paths. The bundled Ansible Self-Service UI uses the new routes automatically.

docs.title: AAP OAuth token in templates (Create Task)
docs.text:
When users run job templates from Self-Service → Create Task, the portal passes the AAP OAuth token to the scaffolder in secrets (for example aapToken). Template steps that invoke rhaap:* actions should pass the token from secrets, for example:

token: ${{ secrets.aapToken }}

Do not rely on a token field in plain template parameters / values for that credential. See the project CHANGELOG for rationale.

docs.title: From Manual Job Template Management
docs.text:
If you're currently managing job templates manually in Backstage:

  1. Enable the sync feature with enabled: true
  2. Configure appropriate filters to avoid duplicates
  3. Remove manually created template entities
  4. Update any references to use the new synchronized templates

docs.title: Upgrading Configuration
docs.text:
When upgrading from older versions:

  1. Review new configuration options
  2. Update sync schedules if needed
  3. Consider adding label-based filtering
  4. Test sync functionality in development environment

docs.title: Users, Teams, and Organizations Synchronization
docs.text: The Users, Teams, and Organizations Synchronization feature automatically imports and synchronizes user accounts, team structures, and organizational hierarchies from Ansible Automation Platform (AAP) into Backstage. This integration ensures that your Backstage catalog reflects your AAP organizational structure and maintains consistent user and group management across both platforms.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
This synchronization feature creates Backstage entities that mirror your AAP organizational structure:

  • Organizations → Backstage Group entities with type organization
  • Teams → Backstage Group entities with type team
  • Users → Backstage User entities with proper group memberships

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Automatic Synchronization: Users, teams, and organizations are automatically imported from AAP on a configurable schedule
  • Hierarchical Structure: Maintains organizational hierarchy with proper parent-child relationships
  • Group Memberships: Preserves team and organization memberships
  • Superuser Management: Creates dynamic aap-admins group for AAP superusers
  • RBAC Integration: Adds AAP-specific annotations for role-based access control
  • Batch Processing: Efficiently handles large user bases with batch processing

docs.title: Basic Configuration
docs.text:
Add the following configuration to your app-config.yaml:

catalog:
  providers:
    rhaap:
      development:
        orgs: Default # Organization name(s) to sync from
        sync:
          orgsUsersTeams:
            schedule:
              frequency: { minutes: 60 }
              timeout: { minutes: 15 }

docs.title: Advanced Configuration Options
docs.text:
catalog:
  providers:
    rhaap:
      development:
        # Single organization
        orgs: Default

        # Multiple organizations
        # orgs:
        #   - Default
        #   - DevOps-Team
        #   - QA-Team

        sync:
          orgsUsersTeams:
            schedule:
              frequency: { minutes: 60 }
              timeout: { minutes: 15 }

docs.title: Configuration Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description orgs string or array Yes Organization name(s) to synchronize from AAP schedule.frequency object Yes How often to sync (e.g., { minutes: 60 }) schedule.timeout object Yes Maximum sync duration (e.g., { minutes: 15 })

docs.title: Multiple Organizations
docs.text:
To sync from multiple organizations, use an array format:

catalog:
  providers:
    rhaap:
      development:
        orgs:
          - Default
          - DevOps-Team
          - QA-Team
        sync:
          orgsUsersTeams:
            schedule:
              frequency: { minutes: 60 }
              timeout: { minutes: 15 }

docs.title: Organization Entities
docs.text:
Organizations from AAP are synchronized as Backstage Group entities:

apiVersion: backstage.io/v1alpha1
kind: Group
metadata:
  namespace: default
  name: default
  title: 'Default'
  annotations:
    backstage.io/managed-by-location: 'url:https://aap.example.com/access/organizations/1/details'
    backstage.io/managed-by-origin-location: 'url:https://aap.example.com/access/organizations/1/details'
spec:
  type: organization
  children:
    - devops-team
    - qa-team
  members:
    - john.doe
    - jane.smith

Key Fields:

  • name: Sanitized organization name (lowercase, spaces to hyphens)
  • title: Original organization name from AAP
  • type: Always organization
  • children: List of team names within the organization
  • members: List of usernames who are direct organization members

docs.title: Team Entities
docs.text:
Teams from AAP are synchronized as Backstage Group entities:

apiVersion: backstage.io/v1alpha1
kind: Group
metadata:
  namespace: default
  name: devops-team
  title: 'DevOps Team'
  description: 'DevOps and Infrastructure Team'
  annotations:
    backstage.io/managed-by-location: 'url:https://aap.example.com/access/teams/5/details'
    backstage.io/managed-by-origin-location: 'url:https://aap.example.com/access/teams/5/details'
spec:
  type: team
  children: []
  members:
    - alice.johnson
    - bob.wilson

Key Fields:

  • name: Sanitized team name (lowercase, spaces to hyphens)
  • title: Original team name from AAP
  • description: Team description from AAP (if available)
  • type: Always team
  • members: List of usernames who are team members

docs.title: User Entities
docs.text:
Users from AAP are synchronized as Backstage User entities:

apiVersion: backstage.io/v1alpha1
kind: User
metadata:
  namespace: default
  name: john.doe
  title: 'John Doe'
  annotations:
    backstage.io/managed-by-location: 'url:https://aap.example.com/access/users/123/details'
    backstage.io/managed-by-origin-location: 'url:https://aap.example.com/access/users/123/details'
    aap.platform/is_superuser: 'false'
spec:
  profile:
    username: john.doe
    displayName: 'John Doe'
    email: 'john.doe@example.com'
  memberOf:
    - default
    - devops-team

Key Fields:

  • name: AAP username
  • title: Full name (first + last name) or username if names not available
  • profile.username: AAP username
  • profile.displayName: Full name or username
  • profile.email: User's email address from AAP
  • memberOf: List of groups (organizations and teams) the user belongs to

docs.title: Superuser Handling
docs.text:
AAP superusers receive special treatment:

apiVersion: backstage.io/v1alpha1
kind: User
metadata:
  name: admin.user
  annotations:
    aap.platform/is_superuser: 'true' # ← Superuser annotation
spec:
  memberOf:
    - default
    - devops-team
    - aap-admins # ← Automatic membership in aap-admins group

The aap-admins group is dynamically created and includes all AAP superusers, enabling RBAC policies based on AAP administrative privileges.

docs.title: Data Flow
docs.text:
1. Organization Discovery: Fetches organizations matching the configured orgs filter
  2. Team Retrieval: For each organization, retrieves all associated teams
  3. User Collection: Collects users from both organization and team memberships
  4. Batch Processing: Processes users in batches of 100 to avoid API overload
  5. Entity Creation: Creates Backstage entities with proper relationships
  6. Catalog Update: Updates the Backstage catalog with new/updated entities

docs.title: Membership Resolution
docs.text:
The sync process handles complex membership scenarios:

  • Organization Members: Users directly assigned to organizations
  • Team Members: Users assigned to teams within organizations
  • Duplicate Handling: Users appearing in multiple teams are deduplicated
  • Membership Tracking: Maintains accurate memberOf relationships

docs.title: Performance Optimization
docs.text:
• Batch Processing: Users are processed in batches of 100 to prevent API timeouts
  • Parallel Requests: Team and user data is fetched in parallel where possible
  • Efficient Deduplication: Uses unique user IDs to avoid duplicate processing
  • Incremental Updates: Only updates entities that have changed

docs.title: Discovering Users and Groups
docs.text:
1. Navigate to Catalog in Backstage
  2. Filter by Kind:
  3. Select User to see synchronized users
  4. Select Group to see organizations and teams
  5. Use the search functionality to find specific users or groups
  6. View entity details to see memberships and relationships

docs.title: User Profiles
docs.text:
Synchronized users appear with:

  • Profile Information: Name, email, username from AAP
  • Group Memberships: Organizations and teams they belong to
  • AAP Links: Direct links to user details in AAP
  • Superuser Status: Visible through annotations and group membership

docs.title: Group Hierarchies
docs.text:
Organizations and teams maintain their hierarchical structure:

  • Organizations show child teams and direct members
  • Teams show their members and parent organization
  • Navigation allows browsing the organizational structure

docs.title: AAP Superuser Integration
docs.text:
The sync creates an aap-admins group containing all AAP superusers:

# Example RBAC policy
policy.csv: |
  p, group:default/aap-admins, catalog-entity, read, allow
  p, group:default/aap-admins, catalog-entity, create, allow
  p, group:default/aap-admins, catalog-entity, update, allow
  p, group:default/aap-admins, catalog-entity, delete, allow

docs.title: Organization-Based Permissions
docs.text:
Use organization groups for department-level permissions:

# Example: Default organization permissions
policy.csv: |
  p, group:default/default, catalog-entity, read, allow
  p, group:default/default, scaffolder-template, use, allow

docs.title: Team-Based Permissions
docs.text:
Use team groups for project-level permissions:

# Example: DevOps team permissions
policy.csv: |
  p, group:default/devops-team, kubernetes-cluster, read, allow
  p, group:default/devops-team, deployment-pipeline, execute, allow

docs.title: Common Issues
docs.text:
Users not appearing in catalog:

  • Check AAP connectivity and token permissions
  • Verify organization names match exactly (case-sensitive)
  • Review sync schedule and logs for errors
  • Ensure users have proper organization/team memberships in AAP

Group memberships incorrect:

  • Check team assignments in AAP
  • Verify organization membership settings
  • Review batch processing logs for errors
  • Ensure AAP API returns complete membership data

Sync performance issues:

  • Adjust batch size if processing large user bases
  • Increase sync timeout for large organizations
  • Monitor AAP API rate limits
  • Consider reducing sync frequency for stable environments

Missing superuser privileges:

  • Verify is_superuser flag is set correctly in AAP
  • Check aap-admins group creation in logs
  • Ensure RBAC policies reference the correct group name

docs.title: Logging and Monitoring
docs.text:
Enable debug logging to troubleshoot sync issues:

backend:
  logging:
    level: debug

Monitor these log entries:

  • plugin-catalog-rhaap: Main sync process logs
  • backstage-rhaap-common: AAP API interaction logs

docs.title: Manual Sync Trigger
docs.text:
To manually trigger a sync (useful for testing):

  1. Access the catalog backend API
  2. Call the refresh endpoint for the AAP entity provider
  3. Monitor logs for sync progress and any errors

docs.title: Token Management
docs.text:
• Use AAP tokens with minimal required permissions (read access to users, teams, organizations)
  • Rotate tokens regularly according to your security policy
  • Store tokens securely using Backstage's secret management

docs.title: Data Privacy
docs.text:
• User email addresses and names are synchronized from AAP
  • Ensure compliance with your organization's data privacy policies
  • Consider data retention policies for synchronized user information

docs.title: Access Control
docs.text:
• Synchronized groups can be used in RBAC policies
  • Superuser status is preserved and can be used for administrative access
  • Regular auditing of group memberships is recommended

docs.title: Organization Structure
docs.text:

docs.title: Picker Content Boundary: Query Dimensions + Write Schema
Portal and content service boundary
docs.text: From: Portal Plugin Factory team To: Content Management team Status: Draft — supersedes previous "operation contract" proposal Context: Content extraction and picker contracts

docs.title: 1. Background
docs.text:
The self-service plugin contains seven scaffolder field pickers. As part of the planned content extraction, these are split by data ownership:

  • Pickers that query Ansible content (collections, EE images) — the content boundary defined in this document. The Content Management team owns the data; we own the picker widget.
  • Pickers that query AAP resources (organizations, inventories, projects) — continue to use existing AAP API routes. Not part of this contract.
  • Pickers that are pure user-input (tags, pip package names, file names, MCP servers, SCM choices) — free text or template-enum. No content boundary. Not part of this contract.

What we are agreeing on here:

  • The query dimensions each picker needs (what fields are queryable on each content type)
  • The write schema (what the template form persists after a picker selection)
  • The authz requirement per query
  • The sourceId stability invariant (non-negotiable — stored values must survive upgrades)

What we are NOT prescribing: how the query is implemented. Whether sources and versions arrive as facets on a search query, relations, or a separate index is the Content Management team's decision. The picker is a widget; we do not own the query engine.

docs.title: The two pickers in scope
docs.text: Picker component Content it queries CollectionsPickerExtension Ansible collections from PAH / Galaxy / OCI BaseImagePickerExtension Built EE images available as base images

docs.title: 2. Current Behaviour (What We Ship Today)
docs.text: Understanding the current implementation makes the required data surface explicit.

docs.title: 2.1 CollectionsPicker
docs.text:
The picker today calls scaffolderApi.autocomplete with three resource strings in a cascade: name → source → version. The user flow is:

  1. Type to search collection names → select one
  2. Select a source (PAH instance, Galaxy, OCI registry) where that collection is available
  3. Optionally select a version at that source (or leave blank for "latest")

The value stored in the template form is:

interface CollectionItem {
  name: string; // e.g. "community.general"
  source: string; // source ID — stored in the EE definition file
  version?: string; // version string, or null for "latest"
}

docs.title: 2.2 BaseImagePicker
docs.text:
Currently static — available base images are hardcoded as a JSON schema enum in the template YAML. No API call is made at runtime.

The planned integration requires this to become dynamic — fetching available base images from the content catalog so that new AAP releases appear automatically without template edits.

The value stored in the template form is:

interface EEBaseImageRef {
  imageRef: string; // fully qualified: "registry/image:tag"
  digest?: string; // sha256:... for reproducible pinning (preferred for production)
}

docs.title: 3. Content Boundary: Query Dimensions + Write Schema
3.1 Collection type
docs.text:
What the picker needs to query:

Dimension Description Notes name Full-text / prefix search on collection name (e.g. "community.general") Powers the first autocomplete sources For a selected collection: what sources carry it (PAH, Galaxy, OCI, etc.) A relation or facet — not a separate RPC. Sources are IDs + human labels versions For a selected collection + source: available versions May be live-fetched or indexed — freshness is the content service's concern, not ours

Write schema (what we store and what must stay stable):

interface CollectionItem {
  name: string; // fully qualified collection name — stable
  source: string; // opaque source ID — MUST survive PAH upgrades (see §4)
  version?: string; // version string, or null/omitted for "latest"
}

Authorization: ansible.collections.view (already declared in backstage-rhaap-common)

docs.title: 3.2 Execution environment image type
docs.text:
What the picker needs to query:

Dimension Description Notes usableAsBase Filter to images that can act as a base image in an EE definition Boolean facet — not all EEs are usable as base imageRef Fully qualified pull reference (registry/image:tag) Written into execution-environment.yml digest OCI digest (sha256:...) for reproducible pinning Optional but preferred for production definitions recommended Whether this is the RH-recommended base for new definitions UI renders a "Recommended" badge; at most one true

Write schema:

interface EEBaseImageRef {
  imageRef: string; // written directly into execution-environment.yml
  digest?: string; // sha256:... for reproducible pinning
}

Authorization: ansible.execution-environments.view (already declared)

docs.title: 4. Non-Negotiable: sourceId Stability
docs.text:
The source field in CollectionItem is stored inside execution-environment.yml files committed to source control. If the Content Management team changes the opaque ID for a source across PAH upgrades (e.g. during a re-registration), existing EE definitions silently reference a source that no longer exists.

We need one of:

  1. A stability guarantee: source IDs are immutable once assigned. Decommissioned sources get a tombstone (still resolvable, marked deprecated) rather than a deletion.
  2. A migration event: an observable signal we can subscribe to when a source ID changes, so we can update stored EE definitions proactively.

This is the single hardest dependency between our teams. Everything else in this document is a fresh build; this one touches committed customer files.

docs.title: 5. Open Questions
docs.text: # Question Impact Q1 Is Collection.providedBy in the current AutomationContentClient the stable source ID, or a display label? Determines whether we can use it as the stored source field. Write schema stability Q2 Is collection/version data served from a live PAH query or from a Backstage Search index (collator)? Determines picker latency, offline behaviour, and whether search is live-typed or request-on-open. UX + freshness model Q3 For usableAsBase — is this a computed field (introspection-derived) or manually curated? Affects whether new Red Hat EE releases appear automatically or require a catalog update. BaseImagePicker accuracy Q4 Is digest always available for catalog-indexed images, or only after a live registry fetch? Reproducibility guarantee

docs.title: 6. What We Commit To (Portal team)
docs.text:
Once the open questions above are answered:

  1. Implementing CollectionsPicker against the agreed query API — the cascade (name → source → version) maps to the declared query dimensions regardless of how the content service implements the underlying query.
  2. Implementing BaseImagePicker dynamic fetching against the usableAsBase filter.
  3. Publishing CollectionItem and EEBaseImageRef in portal-extension-common as the stable write schemas both teams import.
  4. Not coupling picker internals to RHDH APIs. The picker calls our abstraction layer; that layer calls the published content client. When RHDH changes the search seam, we update the adapter — not the picker widget and not the template authors.

docs.title: 7. Non-Content Pickers (Out of Scope for This Contract)
docs.text:
The remaining five pickers have no content ownership dependency:

Picker Data source Ownership after extraction EETagsPicker User-provided free text Stays in portal-scaffolder PackagesPicker User-provided free text (pip package names) Stays in portal-scaffolder MCPServersPicker Static schema enum from template YAML Stays in portal-scaffolder AAResourcePicker AAP API (organizations, inventories, projects) Stays in portal-scaffolder, continues to use AAP proxy ScmSelector Static enum (GitHub, GitLab) Stays in portal-scaffolder; may add Gitea if the content service supports it

The Content Management team is not blocked on any of these five. They are entirely portal-scaffolder owned and require no content boundary agreement.

docs.title: Current delivery scope
docs.text:
The Portal Plugin Factory provides the contracts and SDKs that let first-party and third-party plugins contribute to Automation Portal. This is an experimental implementation, not a claim that the full Content Experience Architecture has shipped.

Currently, native NFS composition and the agreed functional checks are complete. Content extraction and cross-team query/write contracts remain separate work. The upstream review branch is feat/portal-plugin-factory-sdk; anstrat-2497-poc retains the original development history in the fork.

Use Portal NFS composition for the current frontend integration contract. Earlier registry and Scalprum descriptions in historical architecture documents are not instructions for the native app.

docs.title: Internal developer-preview readiness
docs.text:
The internal developer-preview contract defines the proposed API boundary, supported launch subset, backend responsibilities, exclusions, and compatibility policy for consuming teams. Its implemented behavior is distinct from the policy awaiting joint agreement. Preview teams develop plugins in this repository's workspaces using workspace:^ SDK dependencies and the shared root lockfile. Native composition being complete does not mean team onboarding or all architecture requirements are complete; npm publication is not a preview requirement.

Before declaring a consumable preview:

  1. Agree on the documented API subset and breaking-change migration policy with SDK maintainers and consuming teams.
  2. Review the intended consumer's mutation and background-work paths. Migrate paths that bypass the agreed authorization/operation boundary, or explicitly exclude those features; frontend gates alone are not an exclusion mechanism.
  3. Complete the author guide's fresh-clone acceptance with the consuming team's workspace plugin: install dependencies from the root, build/test the required packages, export dynamically, and install the artifacts in RHDH. No external plugin repository or npm publication is required.
  4. Record the SDK revision, dependency versions, RHDH image digest, and tested artifacts. The current deployment baseline remains next-2.1 only.

Broader content extraction, additional launch combinations, and a standalone theme package are separate architecture work. They become preview prerequisites only if the agreed consumer use case requires them. Idempotency deduplication, automatic MCP exposure, and durable auditing are not current dispatcher guarantees; do not advertise them merely because metadata fields exist.

docs.title: Workspace ownership
docs.text:
The repository remains named ansible-backstage-plugins. Package ownership is organized under workspaces/, with one root Yarn workspace configuration and lockfile:

  • portal-core/packages/app and portal-core/packages/backend: development harnesses.
  • portal-core/plugins: shared Portal contracts, host, SDK, operations, and health.
  • self-service/plugins/portal-scaffolder: @ansible/portal-scaffolder, including templates, tasks, and the content pages awaiting extraction.
  • aap/plugins: AAP integration clients, authentication, catalog providers, user provisioning, and scaffolder actions.
  • apme/plugins: the third-party contribution example and its backend modules.

Root plugins/ and packages/ directories no longer contain application code. The WP-001 inventory tool and its inventory:scan script are maintained separately on the fork branch tools/wp-001, not in the SDK branch.

docs.title: Package responsibilities
docs.text:
All Portal packages below live under workspaces/portal-core/plugins/.

  • @ansible/portal-extension-common owns shared manifest, capability, launch, operation, entitlement, and content-type contracts. Runtime predicates belong on frontend descriptors, not in serialized contribution metadata.
  • @ansible/portal-extension-api provides frontend API references, clients, and native Blueprint/data-reference contracts through ./alpha. Its registry helpers remain available for legacy compatibility.
  • @ansible/portal-extension-host validates and filters native descriptors, renders eligible contributions, and supplies error boundaries, design-token wrappers, and an RJSF settings shell. Native adapters are exported through ./alpha.
  • @ansible/portal-core installs the portal frontend plugin's shared contribution, operation, and entitlement APIs. Its ./app-nav module adapts discovered pages into configuration-driven navigation.
  • @ansible/portal-plugin-sdk supplies reusable components, notifications, caching, context hooks, styles, icons, and theme utilities.
  • @ansible/portal-plugin-node supplies backend operation registration, identity/context helpers, audit emission, organization helpers, and health reporting infrastructure.
  • @ansible/portal-operations-backend exposes authorized operation dispatch and server-resolved organization/entitlement decisions.
  • @ansible/portal-health-backend exposes aggregated health at /api/portal-health/status. Backend health reporting does not imply that a health indicator is installed in the application UI.

A standalone portal-theme package is not present. Current shell integration uses Portal navigation, existing theme utilities, and an app-owned global-header wrapper. RHDH keeps its own platform header.

docs.title: Native contribution lifecycle
docs.text:
Plugins declare reusable host-owned Blueprint extensions in static ./alpha entry points. They supply content scope, host attachment regions, permissions, entitlements, and optional narrowing predicates.

The portal frontend plugin installs api:portal/contributions once. The provider collects native descriptors through NFS data references rather than a shared mutable module-load registry. The host validates ownership, contract versions, references, regions, and content scope before activation.

Content/source matching, enabled experiences, configuration, permissions, entitlements, and predicates gate component loading. Only eligible contributions are mounted, inside host error boundaries. Actions dispatch registered operations with the current subject; plugins do not supply handler URLs.

CapabilityLaunch is a discriminated union of slot, workflow, and operation launches, with optional operation follow-on behavior. Although legacy types still contain optional moduleName metadata, the native path does not resolve arbitrary module names imperatively. NFS declarations own component loading.

Host experiences remain content-quality-assessment, content-authoring, and content-migration. Portal scaffolder is a plugin, not a fourth experience. Built-in catalog overview content is not an APME Quality capability.

docs.title: Delivered functional slices
docs.text:
The current native implementation includes:

  • Collections, execution environment, repository, template, task history, and catalog-import routes, without duplicate /portal/* pages.
  • Entity tabs, overview cards, entity actions, catalog item actions, catalog tabs/columns, workflow launchers, and native scaffolder fields.
  • APME Quality, Quality activity, Dependencies, scan actions, Add repository, and manual registration/deregistration.
  • Configurable sidebar links/groups with plugin-owned route/icon metadata. Administration can contain RBAC or link directly to it; Settings is independent.
  • Native RBAC, Settings, Search, and source-app global-header integration, preserving authorization and existing logout behavior.
  • Catalog-removal reconciliation before redirect/refresh, without resubmitting an accepted removal operation.
  • APME-owned summary refresh while background operations remain active.
  • Trusted AAP direct/team memberships intersected with configured organizations, and server-side entitlement grants. Any granted membership enables a shared capability, subject to RBAC; multiple memberships do not select an active organization for organization-specific state.
  • Consistent organization context across operation and registration transports, central enforcement of declared operation entitlements, and authorized APME interactive workflow forwarding. Git repositories remain shared resources; new manual entries use default without AAP ownership annotations or catalog namespace mappings. Existing records are not rewritten.
  • Flag-controlled stable AAP user/group/template identities, aligned across authentication, catalog sync, and the extracted user provisioner. The frontend SDK reads trusted membership context from the backend rather than user namespace.

The legacy app is an explicit ?portalFrontend=legacy fallback. Do not install its side-effect registration entry point alongside native APME declarations.

docs.title: Verification boundaries
docs.text:
Packed dynamic exports were exercised on quay.io/rhdh-community/rhdh:next-2.1 using mock AAP authentication and a local APME gateway. Separately, the source NFS app was verified with real AAP login and completed scan-only operations with persisted findings and automatic refresh.

The named manual test-repository registration was created and removed through native surfaces, preserving the GitHub repository and existing APME history. These checks do not prove real-AAP authentication inside the RHDH container, successful scanning of every repository, or remediation/PR creation.

The closure regression run passed 30 targeted suites and 313 tests, with TypeScript and lint checks passing. This is a previous targeted result, not the current full-repository test count or a guarantee of GitHub CI status.

The current documentation passes the full strict build. Local documentation environments must install the configured theme and support Cairo shared-library discovery for social-card generation; a content-only diagnostic build is not equivalent to the full configured build.

docs.title: Content extraction and picker contracts
docs.text:
Collections, repository browsing, and built-image views still need their agreed content-owned boundary and migration. EE definition authoring and Portal picker widgets retain their appropriate authoring/scaffolder ownership.

The content boundary is a generic query with type-declared fields and a stable write schema, not a private RPC per dropdown. For collection and base-image selection, agree on:

  1. Query fields, source/version facets or relations, and freshness semantics.
  2. Persisted collection selections and image reference/digest schemas.
  3. Stable source IDs that survive upgrades and appear in EE definition files.
  4. Authorization on returned hits and the published client/transport boundary.

AAP-resource pickers remain AAP integration concerns. Free-text/template-enum fields do not block the content boundary. See the content picker contract proposal. It is still a proposal, not a jointly frozen production contract.

docs.title: Production contracts and delivery
docs.text:
Use the preview contract for the bounded internal authoring surface. Its proposed 0.1.x compatibility policy is not a jointly approved supported-release commitment.

Authorization migration remains for legacy mutation routes and automatic background scans. The current interactive checks do not create organization selection, gateway tenancy, or cancellation of already-running work.

Before broader release, agree on contract versioning, compatibility guarantees, and delivery ownership with the consuming teams. Package publication and out-of-tree onboarding are separate future delivery decisions, not prerequisites for this in-repository preview. Complete remaining architecture requirements independently of native UI composition; in particular, do not infer full multi-organization session support or durable audit storage from the current SDK helpers.

Repository renaming to automation-portal-plugins remains deferred pending coordination. The completed workspace move does not mean the repository rename or all planned architecture work is complete.

docs.title: Portal SDK architecture
docs.text:
The Portal SDK lets independently installed plugins contribute functionality to host-owned surfaces. Plugins declare capabilities and typed native frontend extensions; the host validates, filters, and renders them. Backend operations are registered separately so multiple UI surfaces can reuse the same handler.

This page describes the current implementation on the plugin-factory SDK branch. It is an experimental implementation, not a supported release or a claim that the complete Content Experience Architecture has shipped.

docs.title: Host, experience, and contributor
docs.text:
• Host: owns the supported interaction contracts, semantic attachment regions, context, validation, and presentation lifecycle.
  • Experience: a host-owned user goal such as Content Quality, Authoring, or Migration. A plugin is not an experience.
  • Contributor: supplies domain components, predicates, operation handlers, and plugin-owned persistence. APME is the current third-party example.
  • Capability: a plugin's functionality, with one or more entry points such as a summary card, detail tab, or scan action.

Self-service currently supplies the catalog and detail pages. It consumes host adapters without importing APME's implementation. Content browsing still awaits the planned content ownership split.

docs.title: Native contribution lifecycle
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  Declare["Plugin alpha entry point<br/>Blueprint and manifest references"]
  Discover["NFS discovery<br/>Typed descriptors"]
  Validate["Validate<br/>Ownership, versions, references, region, scope"]
  Filter["Filter<br/>Content/source, experience/config,<br/>permission, entitlement, predicate"]
  Load["Load eligible component"]
  Render["Render within host<br/>error boundary and loading lifecycle"]
  Omit["Omit contribution<br/>Diagnostics for invalid declarations"]

  Declare --> Discover --> Validate --> Filter --> Load --> Render
  Validate -->|"Invalid"| Omit
  Filter -->|"Not applicable or denied"| Omit

Entity/catalog descriptors reach the shared provider through stable NFS data reference IDs. Pages read its validated snapshot via portalContributionsApiRef. Scaffolder fields have a separate native input on the templates page; not every Blueprint uses the entity/catalog provider input.

Static declarations load with the plugin. Component loaders remain deferred until eligibility checks pass; a tab component loads when that eligible tab is selected. Runtime predicates narrow the declared scope and cannot broaden it.

There is no native module-load registration into a global mutable ContributionRegistry. The explicit legacy app retains separate compatibility helpers; do not install both registration paths in the native app.

docs.title: Operation execution
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
  participant User
  participant UI as Host action
  participant Client as Portal operations client
  participant Host as Operations backend
  participant Handler as Contributor handler

  User->>UI: Select Scan
  UI->>Client: execute(operationId, subject, input)
  Client->>Host: Authenticated request
  Host->>Host: Resolve caller and trusted organization memberships
  Host->>Host: Check operation permission
  Host->>Host: Validate input schema
  Host->>Host: Enforce declared entitlements for the operation scope
  Host->>Handler: Execute registered handler with context
  Handler->>Handler: Resource checks and domain work
  Handler-->>Host: Result or job reference
  Host->>Host: Validate output and emit audit event
  Host-->>UI: Response
  UI->>UI: Supported follow-on navigation and refresh

The client discovers the portal-operations backend and sends an operation ID, the current subject's entity reference, and optional input. The manifest does not supply a handler URL. A descriptor alone does not install a handler: the backend registers it through portalOperationsServiceRef.

The dispatcher independently resolves trusted memberships, rejects an inconsistent context, and checks operation permission, declared entitlements, and input/output schemas. The handler remains responsible for resource access and domain checks. An accepted scan request is not a completed scan; job progress and findings belong to the contributor.

REST dispatch, identity middleware, repository registration adapters, and APME interactive workflows use the same injected organization resolver. Identity namespace is not organization identity. APME scan operations declare requiredEntitlements: ['apme.scanning']; workflow submission, approval, and state/event routes also enforce entitlement and repository access before forwarding traffic or resolving SCM credentials. State/event reads do not require the scan mutation permission.

The AAP adapter verifies the authenticated AAP identity, resolves current direct organization and team memberships, and intersects them with configured Portal organizations. Entitlement grants control availability, not membership. For a shared repository operation, any granted membership enables the capability; operation and resource permissions must still pass. For example, a user in Engineering and Finance can scan a shared repository when Engineering grants scanning, even if Finance does not.

PortalContext.organizationId is present only when one organization is unambiguous; organizationIds carries multiple trusted memberships without selecting the first. Operation descriptors default to organization-specific scope and require one validated organization. Descriptors explicitly declaring organizationScope: 'shared', including APME repository operations, can execute with multiple memberships. Shared access does not select a partition for organization-specific plugin data.

Git repositories have no mandatory AAP organization owner. New manual entries use the default catalog namespace. The former portal.organization.catalogMappings policy and ansible.io/portal-organization ownership checks are removed; existing records and annotations are not rewritten. Catalog namespace and SCM owner are not substitutes for membership or resource authorization.

The frontend usePortalContext hook reads authenticated host context from GET /api/portal-operations/context; it does not derive organization from the user namespace or fall back to default. The backend independently rechecks authorization rather than trusting browser context.

Important: Frontend filtering does not authorize backend resources. Remaining legacy mutations, automatic scanning policy, and organization selection are separate work; these checks do not introduce gateway tenancy or revoke running jobs.

docs.title: Backend health reporting
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  Backend["Contributor backend"]
  Service["Injected portalHealthServiceRef"]
  Registry["Host health registry<br/>In-process state"]
  HTTP["portal-health-backend<br/>GET /api/portal-health/status"]

  Backend -->|"Push status"| Service --> Registry
  Registry -->|"Read snapshot"| HTTP

Health reporting is independent of contribution rendering. The endpoint aggregates plugin status; it is not a durable history store or a domain job tracker. A frontend health component exists in the host library, but the current deployment intentionally does not install a health dashboard or indicator.

docs.title: Ownership and compatibility boundaries
docs.text:
• RHDH loads exported plugin packages; Portal contracts define what their contributions mean. Platform adapters own discovery and authenticated fetch.
  • Plugins select supported semantic attachments, not CSS selectors or arbitrary runtime module URLs. Host pages own the layout.
  • Operations are separate from presentation. New server effects must use registered operations; remaining legacy mutation paths still need migration.
  • Common metadata must remain serializable. New native predicates belong on executable frontend descriptors, even though legacy contract fields remain.
  • The current manifest requires experienceId. The proposed advisory recommendation and richer host composition preview/activation/rollback model are not implemented by the generic attachments alone.

docs.title: Delivered scope and remaining work
docs.text:
The implementation has native tabs, overview cards, entity/catalog actions, catalog tabs and columns, scaffolder workflow launchers, and native scaffolder fields. APME demonstrates Quality, activity, dependencies, scan actions, repository registration/removal, and background-result refresh.

Do not infer universal launch support from the common launch union. Native entity actions support operations and constrained entity-tab follow-ons; catalog-header workflows use registered scaffolder template descriptors. Other combinations require a supported host adapter.

Remaining work includes content extraction and agreed query/write contracts, authorization migration for remaining legacy routes and automatic background work, remaining operation guarantees, configuration/default-off conformance, published preview artifacts, and repeatable release acceptance. Audit emission currently means structured events, not a durable audit database; idempotent metadata does not provide a persisted idempotency-key mechanism.

Packed dynamic exports were exercised on next-2.1 with mock AAP authentication. Real AAP login and completed scan-only work were verified separately in the source NFS app. These are bounded acceptance checks, not broad platform or remediation compatibility guarantees.
